$comment: Where BillTap is registered to collect and remit sales tax, and how often
each state says to file.
THIS IS THE INPUT TO THE COMPLIANCE CALENDAR, and it starts empty on
purpose. A calendar of filing deadlines for all fifty states would be
fiction: you file where you are REGISTERED, not where you have nexus, and
the frequency is not yours to choose — each state assigns it when you
register, based on expected volume, and revises it as volume changes.
Crossing an economic nexus threshold creates an obligation to register. It
does not create a filing deadline. Until a state appears in this file there
is nothing to file there — which is not the same as nothing being owed, and
the gap between those two is where the penalties live.
Add a state only once you hold a permit for it. Copy the frequency and the
period basis from the registration letter, not from memory.
frequency  monthly | quarterly | semiannual | annual
due_day    day of the month the return is due after a period closes.
The 20th is the most common across states; several use the
last day, the 15th, the 23rd or the 25th. Take it from the
letter — a wrong due_day produces a calendar that is
confidently late.
first_period_end  ISO date of the first period you must file for.
prepayment  some states require a prepayment mid-period above a volume.
Note it here; this tool does not model it.
